## The five things this batch exists to do

**1. A form comes up the road with a heading and four places under it, and it is read out in a room, in daylight, with a date on the door, in the local language, with about nine people in it.** Chapter 0351 puts it on a table; Chapter 0355 reads it out. **The four places are a district, a population, a rota and a share. There is no place on it anywhere for the person the four places are about** — and that finding is already on a page in Chapter 0308 and in a mouth, **so do not improve on it and do not repeat it; what Chapter 0355 does is put the fourth place in the room for the first time and let about nine people find out it was there.**

**2. The fourth place is refused by a household, on day 356, in a kitchen, in about four seconds.** A share is a household's. **A household's days are not a rota, and that is on a page in Chapter 0266 in a different woman's own mouth with a reason of hers that is nine years old, and it is NOT said in Chapter 0356, it is not improved on, and no chapter of this volume may say that the woman of Chapter 0356's sentence is that sentence said differently.** She is not that woman. She is a woman of about fifty-two, new to this manuscript, and the chapter is what puts her on a page.

**3. A man of about thirty-eight at a salt wharf is asked what the column is for, and he answers, and what he says is the name of this volume — AND THIS IS THE ONE INSTRUCTION IN THIS PROMPT THAT A REVIEW WILL CHECK AGAINST EVERY FILE YOU PRODUCE.** Chapter 0357, day 357, a Monday, the forty-second day of the Bare Month, the room over a market, in daylight, with a date on the door, about nine people. **He has put a number in a return four times a year since the winter before the water and has never been asked. The woman of about twenty-nine who keeps a public register asks him, because the register is the thing the column is for and she keeps it.** He answers in the local language, out loud, once, in four to eight words.

> **THE WORDS HE SAYS ARE THE NAME OF THIS VOLUME, AND THEY ARE ON A PAGE IN CHAPTER 0357 AND IN NO FILE ANYWHERE ELSE, AND THAT IS THE POINT.**
>
> **No chapter may state that what he said is the name of anything. The narrator may not say it again. No chapter may print it a second time. No state file, no batch record, no prompt and no outline may record the words — including `state/batch-summaries/volume-08-batch-0001.md`, which is the one you are about to write.** `outline/volume-08.md` §6.5 and §17.12 are the arrangement and they bind you.
>
> **It may not contain:** a name; a weekday; an ordinal for a month; a numeral that is a date on a page; the word on the second slate; the word *holder*; the word *fence*; or any word standing for the mark in the orchard.
>
> **The words it may reach for are ordinary words this manuscript has been using for a hundred and fifty chapters.** Word-bounded, case-sensitive, across all three hundred and fifty chapter files: *filler* 0, *march* 0, *hurdle* 1 in 1 file, *population* 1 in 1 file, *column* 994 in 214, *heading* 101 in 40, *four places* 99 in 35, *correctly* 34 in 24, *return* 113 in 44, *tally* 27 in 13, *whose* 221 in 146, *whom* 41 in 34, *nowhere* 84 in 70, *asked* 4,038 in 348. **A name built out of the zero column is a name that is only new, and a name built out of the high column is made of words four hundred miles of people already use, and the second is cheaper and better.**
>
> **A writer who cannot find the words by Chapter 0357 has eight days, and the answer is that he says less than the outline expected and the volume is better for it.**

**4. A fence is finished, on day 353, a Thursday.** Sixteen posts cut in a copse about four miles the other way; nine in the ground on day 348, a Saturday; four more on day 350, a Monday, making thirteen; **the last three on day 353**; and eleven withies bound with the same cord. **9 + 4 + 3 = 16.** A handcart, a coil of rope, a hazel mallet with its head bound in cord. **Four feet is not a measurement; it is a number the man has in his mouth, and he said so out loud on the Saturday, and a fence is not an account of anything and does not know what it is four feet off.** Nobody sent him. Nobody asks him. **No chapter of this volume may print a different total of posts or withies or days in any two chapters, and no chapter of this volume may measure, dig, count, probe or resolve the mark in the field about four hundred paces behind the fence, and no chapter may join the fence to the mark.**

**5. Four people are on a page as four people, and a party of four is a party of four.** Three said yes in their own words on days 330, 331 and 332. The fourth said no in four words before anybody was asked, on day 329, and came to the door of her room on day 333 and did not come in. **Nobody in this batch may ask any of the four whether it will go. The asking is the volume's midpoint and it is on day 375 and it is not yours.** The word for what they are is at zero across all three hundred and fifty files and stays at zero. **NO CHAPTER OF THIS BATCH MAY COUNT THE DAYS SINCE SHE SAID NO, AT ANY VALUE, IN NARRATION OR IN A MOUTH — counting them turns a refusal into a thing that is running out.**

## The figures, and the two things nobody has to be told twice

**Every value at a chapter boundary is derived. A derived value may be used in a chapter that dates it and may not be attributed to a chapter or to a mouth unless a page carries it. Where two elapsed counts sit in one sentence, the event each is measured from has to be named in the sentence. Where a figure has two plausible anchors, name both anchors in the same sentence. And a figure that comes out at exactly half of the right one is a subtraction taken across the wrong boundary** — which is how *sixteen days* survived in three places for a slate that carried the word for thirty-two.

**NO LEAD PARAGRAPH OF THIS BATCH CARRIES AN INTERVAL FIGURE AT ALL.** `bible/power-system.md` §36.1 is a finding and not a preference: ten leads required to carry four figures each came out as one paragraph written ten times with the numerals changed, and a reader stops on it. **Where a figure is load-bearing it is paid for once, in a mouth, attached to a decision, and again only when it changes.**

## The house, and the two checks this repository did not have until four days of decisions ago

**A narrative paragraph is not wrapped in bold. A scene lead, a date paragraph, a ledger paragraph, a paragraph of stage direction and a coda are all plain.** The bold marks the one speaker in a dialogue, one speaker per section, the two voices alternating, and the quotation marks sit outside the marks: `"**the finding.**"` **A panel is plain, is set as its own short block with its own line breaks, and carries no emphasis marks. This batch has no panel.**

**No chapter may contain more than four consecutive speech paragraphs between the same two people.** Every card names a third party, a task, or a thing carried, and says which of the three it is, and the first paragraph has somebody's hands on something. **Volume 06 breached this in six chapters and every one of the six was in a batch whose own record certified the ceiling as held, so the certification is not the instrument and the card is.**

**A speech paragraph carries one of the manuscript's two speaker markers — a quotation mark or a bold mark — or it is invisible to both checks that measure speech, and a first-person paragraph carrying neither is a fault.** Two of them stood in Volume 07's Chapters 0341 and 0342, in that volume's two loudest chapters, until a review repair gave them the marker, **and the count of paragraphs carrying neither marker is a fault and not a statistic and must be zero. Your record publishes it for each of your ten chapters.** A plain narration paragraph is correct and is not in that count; the count is of a paragraph that is somebody talking and is not marked as talking.

**Your record also publishes, for your own ten files, the count of every set of objects your ten chapters name more than once between them, read in each chapter that names it.** None of this repository's seven checks counts an object, and the volume's last image is an object, and a fence of sixteen posts once stood at three different totals across two chapters of Volume 07 until a review closed it at nine on the Saturday, thirteen on the Monday and three for the Thursday. **The figures that hold across your ten, from `outline/volume-08.md` §20.10, and a chapter may not print a different one: one return, with a heading and four places under it — a district, a population, a rota and a share — and no place for the person; the fence at sixteen cut, nine on day 348, four more on day 350 making thirteen, the last three on day 353, and eleven withies; three notices in this batch, seven in the volume; a party of four of whom three go; the four hundred and forty on eleven miles of flats, and the figure the man of about thirty-eight has in his head is on no page and is printed nowhere; one register, one second slate with a date on it and nothing under it; one folded sheet of road with about nine places on it.**

**A bolded share is not a quality figure and you may not treat it as one.** The measure is the share of a chapter's words inside bold marks — heading line included, `---` rules counted, bold marks counted as nothing, the file split on whitespace. **Your record publishes the figure for each of your ten chapters with that chapter's subject beside it. You set no target, no volume may read its own mean as a quality figure, and no review may certify or fail a volume on a mean.** For reference, on Volume 07's last ten this phase measured 8.4, 10.6, 9.5, 10.3, 10.7, 11.6, 9.3, 8.4, 8.6 and 7.0 per cent, a range of 7.0 to 11.6 and a mean of 9.4, in forty-nine spans, against a house model of Volume 01's 10.4 and a ceiling of about 35 — and the mean fell because six of those ten chapters had an object, a piece of ground or a road for a subject, and **a number is a consequence and not a plan.**

**The word-run check runs across the whole volume and not inside one batch's ten**, because a set of consecutive words can be a motif or a fault and no instrument in this repository separates them. Volume 08's declared motifs, which the check is expected to return and is expected to say which is which: **the four places under a heading; the four-second refusal; a condition stated first; a notice in a hand with four days behind it; the empty barrow; and the fence.** **A sentence of forty words or more may not stand verbatim in more than one chapter of a batch.**

## What this batch is not allowed to become

**It is not allowed to become a quest.** **The word is NOT at zero across all three hundred and fifty files, and the figure that stood here was false: on a word-bounded case-sensitive search it is at two, in two files, `chapters/volume-01/chapter-0019.md:169` in a man's mouth and `chapters/volume-01/chapter-0020.md:165` in narration, both in italics, both about a thing in a wall, and it has been at zero for six volumes.** So the word is available and it is owned, and this volume does not take it, and a writer who reaches for it is reaching for a word a man in Volume 01 used about a different thing in a different room. Nobody is looking for anything. **The page the copy was made from is not fetched, the town four hundred miles inland is not entered, and the eight names at the foot of that hundred-and-forty-year-old page are not read** — and that is a decision of record, taken before you, so that a batch does not spend four chapters building toward a document and then have to invent a reason it does not arrive. **What three people can do about a road in fifty days is walk it, and the volume ends with them still on it.**

**It is not allowed to become a mystery about a document.** The return is a quarterly return with a heading and four places under it, the four places are the four things a return has, and the reason the fourth cannot be filled is that a share is a household's. **No document in this volume is defeated. A document that goes back is the ordinary end of a document and not a defeat, and this one goes out correct.**

**It is not allowed to become Volume 07 with the nouns changed.** The antagonist is **a method** — a man who fills a column in from what he is given, and nobody asks him — and not a document with a secret in it. The Crown's schedule stands and is correct and is never opened. The document this volume is about is a quarterly return that has been filled in four times a year for nine years by a man who has never been asked what the column is for, and **the reason the volume exists is that on day 357 somebody asked him, and the answer was four to eight words long and it is the name of the book.**

**And the last thing, which is the whole of what this volume is about and the only thing you have to be careful of. A reader is going to finish Chapter 0357 and turn the page, and the volume will not tell them what the answer was for, and neither will the state layer, and neither will the next prompt. That is not an omission in the record. That is the record.** A page that costs something to produce is the only instrument this book has left that has not lied to anybody, and the other one is a board nobody has written on since the two hundred and twenty-fifth day of this flood.
